newsitem.title: USA: Texas electricity prices rise with unit outages.
newsitem.headline: Texas electricity prices rise with unit outages.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were talked higher Monday with several unit outages and some marketers caught short on power, industry sources said.

Lower Colorado River Authority shut its 430 megawatt (MW) natural gas-fired Ferguson power plant Friday to repair a leaking boiler tube. The outage of the Marble Falls, Tx., plant was scheduled to last until near Wednesday.
Peak, firm electricity in ERCOT for Tuesday was quoted at $22.00-26.00 from near $20.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) late last week, brokers and marketers said.
ERCOT electricity for delivery in 16-hour blocks over the five business days of the week through October was said to be talked at $21.00-24.00.
November ERCOT electricity was quoted at $19.75-$19.90, while December was assessed at $21.50-22.00 per MWh, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
